Modern slavery is a crime that affects people in the UK and around the world. It involves the deception or coercion of an individual for the purpose of exploitation.

Before approaching a potential victim, seek advice from the Fair Work Agency. This can help protect both the individual and any future investigation.

If there is an immediate risk to life or violence is being used or threatened, call 999.

Types of labour exploitation

Human trafficking

Human trafficking is the movement of a person from one place to another for the purpose of exploitation. A person may be deceived, coerced, threatened, forced or abducted in order to control and exploit them for profit.

Forced labour

Forced labour is when people are made to work, often for little or no pay, through violence and intimidation. Victims are trapped, without the freedom to leave and with no choice over their situation.

Labour abuse

Labour abuse can include:

little or no payment for work

lack of personal protective equipment (PPE)

insufficient breaks

long working hours

Signs of labour exploitation

There are a number of indicators that someone may be a victim of modern slavery or labour exploitation.

Appearance

A person may:

wear the same clothes every day

not be dressed properly for their work, such as no warm clothing or protective equipment

have untreated injuries or injuries they cannot explain

Restricted freedom

A person may:

be unable to communicate freely

have limited contact with family or friends

depend on their employer for work, travel and accommodation

have no passport or identity documents

have no access to medical care

Working conditions

A person may:

be unable to choose when or where they work

work long hours over long periods

have no time off

be forced to work under certain conditions

have no employment contract

Finances

A person may:

receive little or no payment for work

have no access to their money or bank cards

be disciplined through fines

be charged for unwanted services

be in debt for transport or accommodation costs

Behaviour

A person may:

be unfamiliar with the local language

follow instructions from someone else

allow someone else to speak for them

have limited interaction with other people at work or home

not trust authorities

Accommodation

A person may:

not know their home or work address

live in poor or unsuitable accommodation

have no choice about where they live or who they live with

live with groups of workers at or near their workplace and rarely leave

Report labour exploitation to the Fair Work Agency

Online form

Use the online form if you think you or someone else is being abused or exploited.

By phone

0800 432 0804

Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm (except public holidays). You can still call outside of these hours and leave a voice message.

Calls are free.

We can arrange for an interpreter, if needed

By email

contact@fairworkagency.gov.uk
